content:
Apple TV's YouTube channel has shared the full panel recordings from their debut appearance in Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, including "Matchbox The Movie," "Widow's Bay," "Dark Matter," "Mayday," and "Silo." Watch them below.

You can watch all five panels below

Last Saturday (July 25), Apple made its debut in Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con, hosting panels for "Matchbox The Movie," "Widow's Bay," "Dark Matter," "Mayday," and "Silo."

Now, Apple has uploaded the full recordings of all panels to its YouTube channel, where you can watch them all in one place below.

The "Mayday" panel brought together the co-writers, producers, and director of the action comedy film, which stars Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh.

"Mayday" tells the story of a U.S. Navy pilot who is shot down behind enemy lines during the Cold War and then forms an unlikely alliance with an eccentric former KGB agent. It is scheduled to premiere on Apple TV on September 4.

The "Silo" panel featured showrunner, creator, and executive producer Graham Yost, executive producer and star Rebecca Ferguson, as well as cast members Common, Ashley Zukerman, Jessica Henwick, Alexandria Riley, and Tim Robbins.

The panel discussed the currently airing third season, as well as what Apple TV subscribers can look forward to in the fourth and final season.

The "Matchbox The Movie" panel featured stars including John Cena, Jessica Biel, Sam Richardson, Teyonah Parris, and Arturo Castro.

The cast discussed their expectations for the upcoming film, which Apple describes as "a fast-paced, globetrotting adventure about a group of friends who have known each other since childhood. Their lives are upended when their long-lost former leader and CIA undercover agent, Sean (played by John Cena), returns to their small town, inadvertently plunging them into a race against time to save the world."

"Matchbox The Movie" will premiere on Apple TV on October 9.

The "Dark Matter" panel featured stars Joel Edgerton, Jennifer Connelly, Alice Braga, and Dayo Okeniyi, as well as series creator, writer, and executive producer Blake Crouch, co-writer and executive producer Jacquelyn Ben-Zekry, and executive producer Matt Tolmach.

The panel looked back on the show's first season and offered an early preview of the second season, which premieres on August 28.

Finally came the highly anticipated "Widow's Bay" panel. Apple had not pre-announced the attendees, but on the day they brought together showrunner Katie Dippold, director and executive producer Hiro Murai, and cast members Stephen Root, Dale Dickey, Jeff Hiller, K Callan, Kevin Carroll, and Kingston Rumi Southwick.

Matthew Rhys also made a surprise appearance, joining the cast and creative team to look back on the show's breakout success and its impressive 19 Emmy nominations.

Apple TV is priced at $12.99 per month, or it can be subscribed to as part of the Apple One bundle. The platform offers a host of hit series and films, including "Severance," "The Studio," "The Morning Show," "Shrinking," and "Silo."
